_comment: timing_app: of thousands of rules for when to hold SPY, do any come close to its return while holding it less of the time, better than simply holding less? Every combination of the values below is a rule. Rules are ranked on the development years ONLY; the best few of each family (the finalists) are then traded through validation against random timings. Validation numbers are shown for finalists only, so nothing can be picked for how it did there. The holdout is opened once, at the end. Fixed BEFORE the first run (2026-11-15).
_symbols_comment: What's timed, and where money waits when it's out (BIL, a 1-3 month Treasury bill fund, so being out earns what cash really would). Prices adjusted for dividends too (Alpaca's adjustment all), since holding SPY pays them.
_money_comment: A target set at a close is traded at the next open. Each change pays slippage_percent on what's sold and on what's bought. A fractional target (vol_target) is only followed when it's rebalance_band away.
_finalists_comment: A rule can be a finalist if in development it held SPY between min_exposure and max_exposure of the time on average and changed its exposure at least min_trades times. They're ranked by edge: their CAGR less the CAGR of SPY held at the same average exposure every day (the rest in BIL), i.e. what the timing itself added. The top `count` are finalists, at most per_family from one family. Each finalist is compared with random_draws random orderings of its own stretches in and out (same exposure, same number of trades). The leaderboard shows the best `leaderboard` rules.
_families_comment: See TimingRule.hpp for what each family does. Percentages are in percent.
_gates_comment: For each finalist in validation: a Sharpe of at least min_sharpe, at least min_lead_over_random ahead of a random timing of itself, and more made than paid in costs. At the holdout also min_trades and the deflated Sharpe (counting every rule tried).
